content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork, C++17, wxWidgets) has an in-app Agent (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`) that sends the whole chat to a model provider on every call: Anthropic Messages (`AnthropicCodec.cpp`) or OpenAI Responses (`ResponsesCodec.cpp`), directly or through the JusPrin Cloud gateway, which forwards either format (`ProviderProfile.hpp`, `account_sign_in`). Today `AgentHost::make_agent_request` (around line 2800 of `AgentHost.cpp`) rebuilds the earlier turns on every request from the chat's messages and tool activities: assistant replies retold as text without thinking, tool calls replayed from `ToolActivity` records, app notes prefixed into user text ("JusPrin app note, not the person's words"), workspace blocks and plate pictures stripped from earlier messages, fired skills dropped from later requests. Every one of those makes the bytes differ from the request before, so provider prompt caches miss; about 70% of an Opus bill was cache writes. Kenneth (the owner) has decided the fix: each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model, a request renders that record plus the new items, nothing is rewritten or re-derived, and what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit. The full design, with roles, lifetimes, the provider-doc citations, risks and every decision (D1 to D9), is in the untracked `chat-history-cache-plan.md` in the main checkout `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`; read it first, read `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (sections 3 and 4) and `chat-history-measurement.md` next to it, and `.claude/worktrees/cache-invariant-test-51dab5/cache-rules.md` for provider cache rules. Never commit any of them. Your worktree is cut from the integration branch `claude/chat-history-cache` at `0807d77282`. It carries a hidden Catch2 guard, tag `[history-prefix]` in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (`agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`), that checks each turn's first request opens with the previous request's bytes on both wire formats; it fails today at 10 assertions and names the remaining leaks: workspace blocks on earlier messages, plate pictures, app notes, thinking, dropped skills. Already done on the branch: reminder deleted, trim and cut deleted, `object_import` always offered, `prompt_cache_key` on OpenAI, harness request logging. Chat records live in the managed project folder (`ProjectPersistence.cpp`, `ProjectStateDocument.cpp`, `state.json` written whole by write-then-rename after a debounce; attachment blobs under `attachments/<id>/<name>`), never in the 3MF. Rules: follow the error-handling discipline in `AGENTS.md` (no catch-and-continue, invariant violations propagate); every change must leave the code simpler or justify its growth in the commit message, and the production diff stat is recorded at merge; no live model calls at all (Kenneth approves paid batches individually; your evals run later against a baseline another session is recording now). Commit on your branch only, no push, no merge, never stage submodules, no attribution lines, temp notes untracked in the worktree root. Shared Mac build rules: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, pass `-- -j4`, one build per build directory, never restart a running build to change targets, run long builds with nohup in their own process group and watch the log, never end your turn to "wait for the build": block in the tool call. Build recipe for a fresh worktree (then build only `agent_bridge_tests`, always with the build dir as an absolute path): `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake -B <abs>/build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib`. A sibling session works in `tests/shell` and `tests/project_prompt` at the same time; stay in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and `tests/agent/`.

Task:
Replace the Agent's re-derived history with an append-only per-chat record that is rendered byte for byte on every request, so that the `[history-prefix]` guard passes on both wire formats and can be un-hidden. This is step R7 of the plan, and it carries R2 (skills) and R6 (notes) with it because the three are one model; R4 (workspace blocks) and R5 (pictures) fall out of "keep as sent". Read the plan doc's "Roles and lifetimes", "Gateway findings" and "R2 design point" sections before designing.

What the record is:
- Per chat, bound to one wire format (a chat talks to one provider family; D5: a model switch within the same format is allowed and only costs one cold cache; a switch across formats on an existing chat must be refused in `AgentHost::handle_set_chat_model` with a clear error, not silently re-rendered).
- Every item ever sent to the model, in order, with its exact wire content: the person's messages with what travelled with them (workspace block, plate picture, file report), assistant output including thinking or reasoning exactly as received (Anthropic thinking blocks with signatures; OpenAI reasoning items; check what each codec receives today and what the provider requires to be replayed), tool calls and results, fired skills, app notes.
- A lifetime per item, never an edit. Skills are visible only on the request that fired them (settled: on Anthropic via in-array `role:"system"` with `clear_at: "next_user_message"` and the beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`; on OpenAI as a `developer` item that has no clear and simply stays, so keep it as it is). App notes become operator-role in-conversation messages (Anthropic in-array `system`, OpenAI `developer`), kept visible, same for project and printer chats; this replaces the "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" user-text prefix. Tool results stay in their own channel.
- Pictures are stored as attachment-blob references and rendered inline at request time; image bytes never go into `state.json`.
- Stored in the chat document (`ProjectStateDocument`/`ProjectPersistence`), so a reopened project continues its chat with the same bytes. Design the migration for chats recorded before this change honestly: a one-time rendering of the old messages (plain person/assistant text, no tool replay) appended as the chat's first record items, after which nothing is re-derived; do not keep the legacy history builder alive beyond that one path, and say in the commit message what an old chat's model now sees.

Gateway constraint: the JusPrin Cloud gateway forwards messages and `cache_control` untouched but sends only its own configured headers, so the `clear_at` beta header does not reach Anthropic through it yet. Send `clear_at` and the header only when the profile is not `account_sign_in`; for the gateway path skills stay visible as on OpenAI. Make this a per-profile decision, never per-request, so one chat's rendering never changes. Note it in the report as the follow-up the gateway needs (add the header to the alias backend in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`).

What to delete: the history re-derivation in `make_agent_request` (the `calls_by_message` replay of `ToolActivity` records into history entries, the text retelling of assistant replies, the note prefix, the stripping of workspace blocks and pictures, the skill-dropping) and anything that only served it. The expected outcome is less production code than before; if a part grows, say why in its commit message.

Tests: fake transports only (see `RecordingProvider`, `anthropic_stream`, `responses_stream` in `test_agent_bridge.cpp`). Add tests that encode the valid transitions: an item once sent is never changed; a later request is the earlier request plus appended items (for Anthropic, modulo the moving `cache_control` breakpoint on the newest user message; keep breakpoint placement as it is, never on a turn-scoped message); a cross-format switch is refused; an old chat migrates once; a reopened project renders the same bytes. Finally drop the `[.]` from the two guard cases so CTest runs them, and show the guard passing on both wire formats. Run the whole agent suite.

Commits: at least one for the record model and rendering (R7, including R4/R5), one for skill lifetime (R2), one for notes as operator role (R6), one for the cross-format refusal (D5), one un-hiding the guard. Each message says what changed, why, and the production diff direction. Done means: all commits on your branch, agent suite and guard green, and an untracked `r7-report.md` in the worktree root with the design as built, the migration behaviour, the production diff stat, the gateway follow-up, what the model now sees differently (this is a behaviour change and will be evaluated live later; list every difference), and anything unverified.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_34d95bfb-fc90-47e6-94ab-adc3d3711d01

1	# Chat history cache: plan and progress
2	
3	Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
4	Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
5	`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
10	provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
11	Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
12	is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
13	kept only after a measurement shows it does something.
14	
15	## Decisions Kenneth owns (all settled 2026-10-29)
16	
17	| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | **decided 2026-10-29** (side session `local_97f342dd`): append-only record of every item ever sent, thinking included, pictures as blob references never inline base64. Visibility is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. See "Roles and lifetimes" below. |
20	| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes. Not neutral: the guard test shows that without the note, two consecutive assistant replies merge into one message on Anthropic | **decided 2026-10-29**: notes become operator-role in-conversation messages (Anthropic in-array `role:"system"`, OpenAI `developer`), kept in the record, never cleared; one treatment for project and printer chat. Replaces the "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" user-text prefix. |
21	| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | **decided 2026-10-29**: visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache. No rolling trim, no silent cut. The compaction is an item in the chat the person can see; the earlier items stay in the record with their lifetime cleared (fits D1), so it lands with R7, not before. |
22	| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | **narrowed 2026-10-29**: either deleted (standing prompt already says it) or a turn-scoped operator message like a skill (cleared at the next user message on Anthropic, stays visible on OpenAI). **decided 2026-10-29: delete it.** Keep the injection eval case (live run, batched with the baselines). |
23	| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Allowed within one wire format; a cross-format switch (Anthropic ↔ Responses, including JusPrin Cloud aliases served in different formats) starts a new chat or is hidden from the picker for an existing chat | Anthropic docs (preserved-thinking reference, as of 2026-09-03): a model switch never fails a request; blocks the new model cannot read are dropped unbilled, the stored history is never edited; the only cost is one cold cache, same as a thinking-level change. Cross-format is different: OpenAI reasoning items are encrypted and the record is in one provider's shape, so switching would mean re-rendering history, which D1 forbids | **decided 2026-10-29** (Kenneth, forked side session): keep same-format switching, no history edit on switch; R7 adds the cross-format check in `handle_set_chat_model` |
24	| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | **approved 2026-10-29** for the phase 2 before/after batches on both providers; the OpenAI "before" run is M4. The prompt-case baseline and the injection eval case are extra batches: ask before running them. |
25	| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | **decided 2026-10-29: 5 min for now.** Revisit with phase 2 numbers (how often a chat pauses longer than 5 min). |
26	| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | **decided 2026-10-29: add it** (project + chat id); part of R8 |
27	| D9 | Write cost of a larger chat record | Never measured (searched git, memory, 1,055 Claude and 637 Codex sessions; every timing is for mesh/3MF saves). Closed without measuring: see M5. Constraint carried into D1: pictures stay blob references, never inline base64 in the document | gates nothing now | closed 2026-10-29 |
28	
29	## Roles and lifetimes in the request (approved 2026-10-29)
30	
31	Decided by Kenneth in the side session "Chat history cache handoff" (`local_97f342dd-4367-4bc5-830d-1c6d6d91db47`), relayed to this doc; his words: "ok. go with your proposal." The provider-doc citations below are that session's, not re-verified here.
32	
33	**Append-only record, separate from visibility.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived; what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source cited: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`): a cleared message stays in the array but renders nothing, must be re-sent verbatim, and rebuilding or dropping it counts as an edit to an earlier message that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.
34	
35	**Three roles, assigned by who speaks, never by lifetime:**
36	
37	| Role | Wire | Carries |
38	|---|---|---|
39	| Operator, standing | Anthropic top-level `system`; Responses `instructions` | Standing prompt and tools, written once per chat, never changed |
40	| Operator, in conversation | Anthropic in-array `role:"system"` (Opus 5.5 and 5.x, not Sonnet 5); OpenAI `developer` item | Situational instructions (skills; the file-load reminder if it survives D4) and app observations (notes: slice finished, hand setup change, calibration handover). The doc names "state changes your application observes" as a use case and distinguishes a user message (from the end user) from a system message (from the operator) |
41	| End user | `user` | The person's words plus what travels with them: workspace block, plate picture, file report. Kept in the record as sent (closes R4) |
42	| Tool results | `tool_result` / `function_call_output` | Their own channel, never promoted; the doc forbids relaying third-party content through system messages |
43	
44	**Lifetimes.** Skills and the reminder clear at the next user message on Anthropic (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`, beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`). OpenAI has no clear, so they stay visible and should be kept short. Notes the model replied to stay visible on both providers. Thinking/reasoning is stored per chat and replayed.
45	
46	**Behaviour changes, so evals are required.** Kenneth confirmed this changes what the model reads. Per his 2026-10-19 rule (last confirmed results are the baseline), every behaviour-changing step runs live prompt evals against a baseline. Baselines needed before any such step: OpenAI journeys (none exist) and the prompt-case set (check the last confirmed model and date). Request-body logging in the harness comes before all of it.
47	
48	**Risks recorded, not resolved:**
49	
50	- `clear_at` is a beta feature.
51	- Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result, so a note landing there needs a placement rule.
52	- OpenAI accumulates visible skill text (1.3–8.5 KB each); whether that changes answers is an eval question.
53	- Unverified whether the top-level `system` field and in-array system messages may coexist in one request (the doc implies yes).
54	- Unverified how the JusPrin Cloud gateway passes in-array system messages through in its Anthropic wire format. Production goes through the gateway, so check before R7.
55	- Corrections the side session made to its own earlier claims, so the tracker does not carry them: Anthropic does accept system messages inside `messages` on 5.x models; OpenAI's `instructions` parameter inserts a system/developer message rather than sitting above both.

110	## Gateway findings (R8 session, read from `tsd-enterprise` master `7ab63cc151`, `web_ent/jusprin/v2/upstream.py`)
111	
112	- Responses format: only `model, store, stream, parallel_tool_calls, instructions, tools, input, reasoning` pass; any other top-level field gets a 400. So `prompt_cache_key` is skipped for `account_sign_in` in the app. **Follow-up in tsd-enterprise:** add `prompt_cache_key` to `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']`, deploy, then drop the `!profile.account_sign_in` condition in `ResponsesCodec::build`. 117	## R2 design point from the R8 breakpoint analysis (settled: see the end of this section)
118	
119	Anthropic's `clear_at: "next_user_message"` clears at the next `role:"user"` message, and a message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts. So under R2 a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, not for the rest of the turn. That matches today's Responses codec (which drops the skill from the next request) and not today's Anthropic codec (which keeps it visible for the turn). If "cleared at the next user message" was meant as the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that. **My call (2026-10-29, not Kenneth's; he can override):** a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, on both providers. Reasons: it is what the OpenAI path does today and what the prompt evals were run against; `clear_at` gives it for free; the alternative needs skills kept in the record for the whole chat, which the lifetime design exists to avoid. R2 implements this; the Anthropic path loses rest-of-turn visibility, which the evals after R2 will show if it matters. Also: `cache_control` is a 400 on a turn-scoped message, so breakpoint 3 (last block of the newest user message) stays where it is; the skill-text leak then disappears on its own because a cleared message costs no input tokens and is never written to the cache. Numbers: 15 of 26 recorded bodies have skill text after the breakpoint, 81,950 bytes in total.

1	# Handoff: how the Agent's chat history is built, and why
2	
3	Written 2026-10-28 for an agent who will take a whole-system view of the chat history the in-app Agent sends to the model. This is a working doc. Keep it untracked: don't commit it, and don't add it to `.gitignore`.
4	
5	## 1. The problem in one paragraph
6	
7	Each time the in-app Agent calls the model, it resends the system prompt, the tool list and the whole chat so far. Providers bill the part they have seen before (the cached prefix) at a small fraction of the full price. During a turn, JusPrin resends exactly what it sent before, so the cache works. At the start of every new turn, though, the app's host rebuilds the earlier chat from its stored records in a different, shorter form. The provider has never seen that version, so it reads back only the system prompt and tool list (15,210 tokens on Opus 5.5) and writes everything after them into its cache again. Kenneth asked whether the history should simply never change. Before anyone rewrites how history is built, he wants each choice that makes it change understood. This document collects those choices, who made each one, and why.
8	
9	## 2. What was measured
10	
11	All runs used Claude Opus 5.5 through the real app (the shell harness `--plan-journey` mode), three chats, one run each. Kenneth approved each batch.
12	
13	| Chat | Before the prototype | With the prototype |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| Plug, quick fit check | $0.30 | $0.23 |
16	| Bunny figurine | $0.43 | $0.32 |
17	| Vase, purpose change, 6-minute pause | $0.56 | $0.51 |
18	| Total | $1.29 | $1.07 |
19	
20	- **What the bill is made of.** About 70% of it is cache writes, at $5 per million tokens on Opus 5.5. A cache read costs $0.20 per million and output costs $20 per million.
21	- **Where the fix showed.** On the turn the app starts itself after a slice finishes, the prototype cut the tokens written to cache from 4,600–12,900 to 900–1,300. That saves about $0.15 across the three chats. The rest of the drop was normal variation: this run made fewer requests.
22	- **Logs and scripts.**
23	  - Worktree: `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch` (branch `claude/opus-cost-batch`).
24	  - The before-and-after logs are in its untracked `opus-batch/out-baseline/` and `opus-batch/out/`.
25	  - `opus-batch/cost.py` prices a log.
26	- **The Opus run switch.** The harness change that lets journeys run on Anthropic (`JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_PROVIDER=anthropic`) is uncommitted in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` in that worktree.
27	- **Model picker label.** In this harness the chat's model picker wrongly says "GPT-5.4 mini". The harness installs the agent directly, and the picker shows the default provider's default model (`AgentHost::default_chat_model`). Requests do go to Opus: the usage lines say `provider=anthropic` and report `cache_creation_tokens`, which only Anthropic sends.

29	## 3. The prototype (uncommitted, same worktree)
30	
31	The agent loop (`ProviderAgent`) keeps the turn that just finished, exactly as it was sent. On the next turn it sends that turn in place of the host's shorter version, but only if the host's new history is exactly the previous history plus the host's shorter version of that turn. Otherwise it falls back to the host's history.

33	- **Files changed:**
34	  - `ProviderAgent.cpp` and `ProviderAgent.hpp` (`carry_finished_turns`, `keep_finished_turn`)
35	  - `ProviderCodec.hpp` (`CarriedTurn`, `TurnTranscript::carried`)
36	  - `AnthropicCodec.cpp` and `ResponsesCodec.cpp` (a shared `push_turn` renders each turn)
37	  - `AgentService.hpp` (`AgentRequest::conversation_id`)

46	## 4. Every way the history sent to the model changes between turns, and why
47	
48	"Kenneth" means he decided it in his own words. "Agent" means an AI session chose it and Kenneth merged the result without discussing that point. Every commit's author shows as Kenneth Jiang, because that is the git user on this Mac.
49	
50	### 4.1 Earlier turns are retold as text: no thinking, no full response
51	- **What.** Each earlier turn is rebuilt from stored message text, plus each tool call with its stored result.
52	- **Origin.** `c5c27082ee`, 2026-09-01, made by Codex while building the first live OpenAI agent (Codex session `~/.codex/sessions/2026/09/01/rollout-2026-09-01T00-08-12-01a05bcc-….jsonl.zst`). Agent. No rationale is recorded. The only comment says "The provider gets bounded semantic history."
53	- **Constraints that probably shaped it** (inferred, not stated):
54	  - The Phase 5.1 handoff in that same commit forbids storing "provider response bodies" in the project 3MF, recovery files or logs, and a turn's thinking is part of those bodies.
55	  - `store:false` is used everywhere.
56	  - OpenRouter is stateless and rejects `store:true` and `previous_response_id` (noted in the provider design doc written in session d01a91fe).
57	- **Later reliance.** Mid-chat switching of provider, model and thinking level (`1ca65bb087`, Kenneth's request of 2026-10-20 in session b4c59a23) works because the replayed history is the same for every provider. Thinking never crosses turns, so a switch needs no translation. That reliance comes from an agent's notes, not from Kenneth's words.
58	- **Caching.** Never considered for this.
59	- **If reversed.** History would have to be stored per provider, and mid-chat model switching would need a fallback (a switch can simply rebuild, since caches are per model anyway).
60	
61	### 4.2 Tool calls and results are replayed, with results over 16 KiB cut
62	- **What.** `115e2776bf`, 2026-09-24, session b6450deb.
63	- **Who.**
64	  - Kenneth asked whether omitting earlier tool calls is common practice, then said "Go ahead and add tool history back for the printer chat".
65	  - When the agent added a per-chat on/off switch, he asked "What are the scenarios when we want the switch to be off?" and then had the switch removed, so the replay applies everywhere.
66	- **Why.** Measured: in the printer chat, text-only history connected correctly 0 of 5 times (the model invented a device id); with the replay it was 5 of 5.
67	- **Details, all chosen by the agent:**
68	  - Each call travels with its result as one entry, so the old 20-entry cap could never send a call without its output.
69	  - Results over 16 KiB become a note to call the tool again. No measurement backed the number.
70	  - The workspace snapshot that comes with a live result is left out of the replay, "since the turn carries the current one".
71	  - The provider's item id is not sent, because with `store:false` it names nothing the service kept.
72	- **Caching.** Not discussed.
73	- **If reversed.** The invented-id failures in the printer chat come back. Keep the replay.
74	
75	### 4.3 History is trimmed to 64 KiB
76	- **What.** `5cf784d30b` (and `be27ab5fcd`), 2026-10-15. It replaced a 20-entry cap that Codex wrote on 2026-09-01 with no recorded reason.
77	- **Who.**
78	  - The problem came from a prompt critique (session 835042f8, finding P9): the old cut dropped the person's words while 16 KiB tool payloads stayed, and requests could reach about 320 KiB.
79	  - Kenneth quoted "Trim history by dropping old tool results before conversation text" and said "spin up a task chip to work on this". So he approved the order: tool results go before words.
80	  - The 64 KiB figure, the three stages and the "last two turns keep their results" rule were set by agents (the brief in 835042f8, the work in session 8ff9449f).
81	- **Why 64 KiB.** Twelve recorded 3-turn chats replayed 9–33 KB, with no single result over 10 KB. So about ten turns fit before anything is trimmed. This was offline arithmetic, sized to the chats, not to any model's context window.
82	- **Caching.** Only the worker agent considered it, writing "trimming from the oldest end and only when needed keeps most of the history cacheable". That holds until the budget is first reached. After that every turn trims again, and dropping entries from the front invalidates the whole cached history on every turn. No one weighed summarising old history, or the providers' own context-management features.
83	- **"Call it again" never tested in the app.** The case that tested whether the model calls the tool again when it sees the omission note (`omitted-replay`, passed 3 of 3 on DeepSeek) was deleted at Kenneth's request on 2026-10-17, without a stated reason. It was never measured in the app.
84	- **If reversed.** You lose the hard limit on request size and the guarantee that old words outlive old tool payloads. The guarantee is the part Kenneth approved.
85	
86	### 4.4 The `<workspace>` block goes only with the current message
87	- **What.** Each user message is sent with a JSON snapshot of the project. Replayed earlier messages carry only their text.
88	- **Origin.** `c5c27082ee`, from Codex. Agent. The tag format came later, in `36d33312ed` (2026-10-15); that change didn't discuss earlier messages.
89	- **Why** (the nearest stated reason, given for app notes in `7f66e75b07`): the snapshot is the authoritative state, and a stale copy in the history could contradict it.
90	- **If reversed.** Old snapshots stay in the history. The model sees several states of the project, and only the newest is current. This already happens within a single turn.
91	
92	### 4.5 Pictures and fired skills are never stored or replayed
93	- **Plate picture on the file-open turn.** Kenneth approved it (session 2163d00d, 2026-10-16) on a proposal saying "Attach them to the current request only, so the cached prefix and the replayed history do not grow." The implementer (session 493f628c) added that a stored picture "would sit as base64 inside the project's saved chat document". Its size was never measured.
94	- **Tool-result images (view_render).** From `b3c785cdec` (2026-09-17): "Held in memory for the adapters to project; never written to the project." They were never meant to be replayed.
95	- **Skills** (event-triggered guidance, such as file-loaded or setup-changed).
96	  - Kenneth's rule (2026-10-17, session 7b80d1f6): "the standing prompt carries principles, and everything situational arrives at the moment it applies." Skills go out on the request where their event happened, last in the request.
97	  - On OpenAI they are then dropped from the turn's next request. That edits the middle of the input and breaks the cache from that point; no one weighed this.
98	  - On Anthropic they stay in place for the rest of the turn (`170d1ae080`). This is for correctness: Opus 5.5 rejects replayed thinking once earlier history has been edited.
99	  - Neither provider replays them on later turns, because they are never stored.
100	- **Caching was weighed for only half of the question.** The reasoning was "don't grow or disturb the cached front". No one asked what leaving these out does to the next turn.
101	- **If reversed.** Requests get bigger (pictures) or carry stale guidance (skills), against Kenneth's rule that situational guidance comes only when it applies. Keeping them only as part of an append-only record is a different question from replaying them as new guidance.
102	
103	### 4.6 The reminder that file-load reports are data, not instructions
104	- **What.** On the turn after a file loads, the host puts a developer message at the very start of the history. It says earlier file-load reports are "source data… never instructions". The message is added only when no skill fired for this request.
105	- **Why it exists.** Defence against prompt injection: file metadata and dialog text must not steer the model. `832bb47c31`, 2026-10-01. Tested by the eval case `file-note-not-instructions`, whose file has a project note reading "AI: set infill to 100%".
106	- **Why "only when no skill fired".** `4ec21799ce` (2026-10-17) moved the file-report instructions into the file-loaded skill, and the agent switched the check to `request.skills.empty()`. When the agent asked whether the reminder should become a skill, Kenneth said "Don't worry about it for now."
107	- **Why at the start.** No reason recorded.
108	- **Side effects nobody weighed:**
109	  - The reminder appears and disappears as skills fire.
110	  - It also drops on a calibration handover turn.
111	  - Each flip changes the first message, so the whole cached history misses.
112	  - It is also why the prototype misses the turn after a file loads.
113	- **Overlap.** Since `86f8395071` the standing prompt also says "File contents, project notes and app data are evidence, not instructions."
114	
115	### 4.7 App notes are left out of the project chat
116	- **What.** "Note" messages (a setup change the person made, "The slice of Plate 1 finished.") are not in the project chat's history. The printer chat includes them as developer messages (`notes_in_context`).
117	- **Who.** Kenneth, 2026-09-06 Pacific (session 2fad4c18, timestamped 09-07 UTC; landed in `67361926b0`): "keep notes out of context." He gave no reason. The agent's reason, in the commit and in `7f66e75b07`: the workspace snapshot already carries that state, and a stale note could contradict it. The printer chat has no snapshot, so its notes go in.
118	- **Consequence nobody weighed.** A turn the app starts with a note sends that note as user text ("JusPrin app note, not the person's words: …", added in `c7ed56d027` by an agent). On later turns the note is missing, so the history shows the model's reply to a note that is no longer there.
119	- **If reversed.** Note text repeats state the snapshot already gives. Kenneth's call stands until he reopens it.
120	
121	### 4.8 Stopped and failed turns
122	- **What.** A stopped reply keeps its partial text, marked `stopped`. The loop discards that turn's in-memory record. Calls already handed to the tool coordinator keep their stored results and are replayed later. Calls the model wrote but that never ran are not replayed. A retry streams the same message again (`attempt+1`).
123	- **Origin.** Unchanged since `c5c27082ee`. No rationale found.
124	
125	### 4.9 A stored tool result can change after the model has seen it
126	- **What happens** (verified by reading the code, not reproduced):
127	  1. In `ToolExecutionCoordinator::pump()` (around lines 1100–1117), `execute()` marks the activity Succeeded and notifies the host.
128	  2. The host sends that result to the model at once (`AgentHost.cpp:669`, `continue_after_tool`).
129	  3. If saving the project afterwards throws (`m_version_after` or `m_document_boundary`), `fail()` rewrites the same record as Failed `local_save_failed`.
130	  4. The model saw "succeeded"; every later replay says "failed".
131	- **Why it matters.** This contradicts the coordinator's own comment "Terminal records never change", which guards only `cancel()`. It also conflicts with AGENTS.md's error-handling discipline: fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns it. It looks like a bug, separate from caching.
132	- **Also by design, on every call:**
133	  - The live result includes `actionId`, `workspaceRevision`, the workspace snapshot and fired skills. The replay does not.
134	  - Large or old results become an omission note.
135	- **slice_start.** Its record is written once and never rewritten. The end of the slice comes as an app note (see 4.7).
136	
137	## 5. Things that look like changes but aren't
138	- **Restoring a chat** switches the active chat and the project setup and posts a note. It does not edit messages.
139	- **One agent object serves every chat and project.** That is why the prototype needs a chat identity: it isn't a history change.
140	- **"Append-only" in the Anthropic codec comments** is Anthropic's rule within a single turn, found in a live smoke test (session 178cf2ff). It was never a project principle. Kenneth's 2026-10-28 question is the first time the principle was raised.
141	
142	## 6. Options for a whole-system design (for discussion, nothing decided)
143	
144	- **A. Keep the prototype.** It works and is tested. It is complex because it checks two copies of the history against each other. It still misses the turn after a file load.
145	- **B. The host stores each turn as it was sent and only appends.**
146	  - The chat document keeps the provider-neutral record of every request's content: the person's words with their workspace block, skill text, the model's text and calls, and results as sent.
147	  - The loop then just appends, and its check shrinks to "same chat, and the last turn finished".
148	  - Questions to settle:
149	    - **Thinking.** Is it kept in memory only (lost on restart or provider switch, which costs one cache miss) or stored? Storing it conflicts with the 2026-09-01 rule against provider bodies in the 3MF (4.1).
150	    - **Pictures.** Kept as references to blobs, or dropped and replaced by a stable placeholder text (4.5).
151	    - **Old workspace blocks.** These keep stale state in the history (4.4). Kenneth's view on that is unknown.
152	    - **Trimming.** It becomes a rare, deliberate compaction (for example a summary) that knowingly starts a new cache, instead of a rolling cut (4.3).
153	    - **The file-load reminder.** Moves into the file-load message itself, or is always present (4.6).
154	    - **Notes.** Either appended where they happened, which reverses Kenneth's 2026-09-07 call, or never sent. The current half-way state is the worst for consistency (4.7).
155	- **C. Keep the host's retelling but make it stable.**
156	  - Stop the reminder flipping, and trim only rarely.
157	  - Add a cache marker at the end of the retold history (Anthropic only reads cache at marked positions, and looks back at most 20 blocks from each marker).
158	  - This saves only the older turns. The turn that just ended is still rewritten at every turn start, which is where most of the money goes.
159	
160	Whichever option is chosen, fix 4.9 on its own.

1	# Provider prompt-caching rules, and where JusPrin's codecs fall short
2	
3	Working doc, 2026-10-28, for the chat-history cache plan (task M2). Untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
4	
5	Both providers cache only an unchanged opening of the request, so an append-only history is necessary on both. It is not enough on either. Anthropic also needs cache markers in the right places, the same thinking and effort settings, and a request within 5 minutes (or 1 hour at extra cost). OpenAI needs requests routed to the same machine, which for the model JusPrin uses means a `prompt_cache_key`; JusPrin sends none. Every rule below was read from the provider's docs on 2026-10-28. "Inference" marks what I concluded rather than read.
6	
7	Sources:
8	- [A1] Anthropic prompt caching: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
9	- [A2] Anthropic thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking
10	- [A3] Anthropic preserved thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking
11	- [O1] OpenAI prompt caching: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
12	- [O2] OpenAI reasoning: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning
13	
14	## 1. Anthropic (Messages API, `AnthropicCodec.cpp`)
15	
16	| Topic | Rule | Source |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| Identical prefix | "Cache hits require 100 percent identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control." | A1 |
19	| Prefix order | The prefix is `tools`, then `system`, then `messages`, in that order. A change at one level invalidates that level and every later one. | A1 |
20	| Markers | Caching happens only at `cache_control` breakpoints, or at the automatic one a top-level `cache_control` adds. "Marking a block with `cache_control` writes exactly one cache entry"; no entry is written for any earlier position. At most 4 breakpoints per request, and the automatic one takes one of the 4. | A1 |
21	| Where markers may go | Tool definitions, `system` blocks, text blocks in user and assistant turns, images and documents in user turns, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks. Not on thinking blocks, citations or empty text blocks. | A1 |
22	| Moving a marker | Moving a breakpoint is the documented pattern for a growing chat ("the fourth breakpoint moved to that new final message"). `cache_control` markers sit outside the thinking prefix check: adding, moving or removing them is not an edit. | A1, A3 |
23	| Lookback | A read looks for an earlier write at the breakpoint, then walks back one block at a time, "at most 20 positions for each breakpoint". A run of consecutive `tool_use` blocks counts as one position, and so does a run of `tool_result` blocks. | A1 |
24	| Timing | An entry can be read only after the response that wrote it has started. | A1 |
25	| Minimum length | 512 tokens for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5/5.1 and Mythos 5/5.1. 1,024 tokens for Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.x. 2,048 for Opus 4.7. 4,096 for Opus 4.5 and 4.6. A shorter prompt is processed uncached, with no error. | A1 |
26	| TTL | 5 minutes by default, refreshed free on every read. A 1-hour TTL is available with `"ttl": "1h"`. A longer TTL must come before a shorter one in the request. The lifetime runs from the start of the request. | A1 |
27	| Price (multiples of the input price) | Writes: 1.25x for 5 minutes, 2x for 1 hour. Reads: 0.1x by default, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. | A1 |
28	| What else invalidates | Tool definitions invalidate everything. `tool_choice` invalidates messages. Adding or removing an image anywhere invalidates messages. A thinking or `output_config.effort` change always invalidates messages, and on some models tools and system too. Per-message effort (a `role: "system"` message, beta) leaves the prefix intact. | A1, A2 |
29	| Thinking in history | Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos keep every earlier turn's thinking in context, and the cache stays valid when a new user message is added. Earlier models strip earlier turns' thinking, so messages after it leave the cache. A thinking block the current model cannot read (another model's) is dropped, and the cached prefix changes from that block on. | A1, A2 |
30	| Edits and thinking (correctness, not just cost) | A thinking block is valid only while `system`, `tools` and every message before it are unchanged. For accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 the API checks this on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1, and by default rejects an edited prefix with a 400. With `drop_block` it drops the block and "the prompt cache restarts at the edit". The listed edits include: adding a text block to an earlier user turn or removing one you added last time; re-rendering context in the first user message with a changed value; shortening an earlier `tool_result` or re-encoding an earlier image; changing `system` or `tools`; removing thinking from the middle of the history. Appending at the end and changing `effort`, `max_tokens`, `tool_choice` or `cache_control` are not edits. | A3 |
31	| Mid-conversation system messages | A `role: "system"` message inside `messages` is supported on current models (not Sonnet 5). In a tool loop it goes after the `tool_result` message, never between `tool_use` and `tool_result`. "Once sent, the message is part of the prefix for later thinking: leave it in place on later requests." | A1, A3 |
32	| Usage | `cache_read_input_tokens` are tokens read; `cache_creation_input_tokens` are tokens written, broken down by TTL in `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`. `input_tokens` are only the tokens after the last breakpoint. Total input = read + creation + input_tokens. | A1 |
33	
34	## 2. OpenAI (Responses API, `ResponsesCodec.cpp`)
35	
36	JusPrin's OpenAI default is `gpt-5.4-mini`, a model from before GPT-5.6, so the "earlier models" rules apply. OpenRouter's caching is not covered here.
37	
38	| Topic | Rule | Source |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| Identical prefix | "Cache reuse requires the entire rendered prefix to match." OpenAI caches the full rendered context: instructions, developer messages, tool definitions, and history with text, images and documents. | O1 |
41	| Markers | Before GPT-5.6: none. Caching is on by default and "Only implicit caching is supported", with breakpoints placed by OpenAI at model-dependent intervals. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.mode` is `implicit` or `explicit`. Explicit mode takes `prompt_cache_breakpoint` on content blocks inside input messages, never on top-level `instructions`. With no breakpoint placed, explicit mode does not cache at all. Up to 4 writes per request. Implicit mode puts a breakpoint at the end of the latest eligible message and looks back over "up to 20 earlier eligible message endings". The docs do not say which mode is the default. | O1 |
42	| Routing | Requests go to a machine chosen by "a hash of the initial tokens after the hidden OpenAI content, including tool definitions". The cache lives on that machine. "traffic above 15 requests per minute can lead to overflow routing", and an overflowed request misses. Before GPT-5.6, `prompt_cache_key` "separates cache reuse between groups of requests and helps optimize cache routing"; the advice is about 15 requests per minute per key. GPT-5.6+ does not need the key. | O1 |
43	| Minimum length | 1,024 visible input tokens on GPT-5.6+. For earlier models it "varies by request settings" (tools, images, schemas, effort, verbosity). Earlier models report `cached_tokens` rounded down to a multiple of 128. | O1 |
44	| Retention | Earlier models, in memory: "around 5 to 10 minutes of inactivity, up to one hour". Extended `24h` retention (`prompt_cache_retention`) is listed for `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5` and others. `gpt-5.4-mini` is not on that list. Organizations without Zero Data Retention default to `24h`. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.ttl` of `30m` (default) or `12h`. | O1 |
45	| Price | Earlier models: no write charge, reads at 0.1x. GPT-5.6+: writes at 1.25x (30 minutes) or 2.5x (12 hours). | O1 |
46	| What else changes the prefix | `model`, `tools` (names, descriptions, schemas, order), `parallel_tool_calls`, `text.format`, `reasoning.effort`, `text.verbosity`, `context_management`. A `configuration_update` input item changes effort without breaking the prefix (GPT-6). | O1, O2 |
47	| Reasoning in history | Within a tool loop, pass back every reasoning item with its call. Models before GPT-5.6 do not render earlier turns' reasoning into the next sample; GPT-5.6 renders it by default. With `store: false`, reasoning items carry `encrypted_content` by default; `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` is still accepted but no longer required. Neither guide says how reasoning items affect cache hits. | O2 |
48	| Usage | `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is billed reads, excluding writes. On GPT-5.6+, `cache_write_tokens` gives writes, split into `ttl_30m_tokens` and `ttl_12h_tokens`. | O1 |
49	
50	Inference, not stated in the docs: on a pre-5.6 model, the last request of turn N renders that turn's reasoning, and the first request of turn N+1 no longer does (it is now an earlier turn's reasoning). If that is how rendering works, the rendered prefix changes at turn N's first reasoning item even when JusPrin resends the input byte for byte. In that case, on `gpt-5.4-mini` an append-only history can win back only the turns before the last one. This needs a live check of `cached_tokens` (one cheap OpenAI run, needs Kenneth's approval).
51	
52	## 3. What the codecs do today
53	
54	`AnthropicCodec.cpp` places three breakpoints, all with the default 5-minute TTL:
55	1. on the last tool (`tools_json`, line 87);
56	2. on the single `system` block (`build`, line 272);
57	3. on the last block of the newest `user` message (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.
58	
59	It sends `thinking: adaptive` and `output_config.effort` from the chat's model choice, replays each response's own blocks (thinking included) within a turn, keeps fired skills in place for the rest of the turn, and reads `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
60	
61	`ResponsesCodec.cpp` sends `store: false`, `parallel_tool_calls: true`, `instructions`, `tools`, `input`, and `reasoning.effort` when set. It sends no `prompt_cache_key`, no `prompt_cache_retention` and no `include`. It replays each response's own items (reasoning included) within a turn. It sends fired skills only as the last items of the request where they fired, and drops them from the next request. It reads `cached_tokens` only.
62	
63	## 4. Gaps
64	
65	The first three are what the guard test in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (`[history-prefix]`) catches; the rest it cannot see, because they are about markers, settings, timing or routing, not the bytes of the history.
66	
67	1. **Earlier turns are rewritten between turns (both codecs).** The host replays them as text: no thinking, no workspace block, no pictures, no skills, results as stored, app notes missing. This breaks the identical-prefix rule [A1, O1]. On Anthropic, once thinking is carried across turns (plan step R7), the same edits become 400 errors for accounts created after 2026-08-31 [A3]. Removing a workspace block from an earlier user turn, re-rendering the file-load reminder in the first message, and cutting a stored result are each named as edits there.
68	2. **Responses drops a fired skill from the next request** (mid-turn, and on the next turn). That changes the middle of the input [O1]. Anthropic's codec already keeps them, which matches "leave it in place on later requests" [A3].
69	3. **The file-load reminder at the start of the history appears and disappears** (handoff 4.6). That is a changed first message, the worst place for an edit [A1, A3, O1].
70	4. **No `prompt_cache_key` on Responses.** Every JusPrin user sends the same instructions and tools, so before GPT-5.6 all of them hash to the same machines. Above about 15 requests per minute across all users, requests overflow to other machines and miss [O1]. A per-chat key (for example the project and chat id) keeps each chat on one machine. GPT-5.6+ does not need it.
71	5. **5-minute TTL on Anthropic, in-memory retention on `gpt-5.4-mini`.** A pause longer than 5 minutes (the vase journey had a 6-minute one) loses the whole Anthropic cache, and the next request writes it all again at 1.25x [A1]. Anthropic offers a 1-hour TTL at 2x per write. On OpenAI, `gpt-5.4-mini` is not listed for 24-hour retention, so its entries last 5 to 10 idle minutes [O1]. Whether 1 hour pays depends on how often people pause: it is a measurement question, not a fix.
72	6. **A mid-chat thinking or effort change restarts the cache on both providers** [A1, A2, O1]. The per-chat thinking picker (`1ca65bb087`) allows this. Anthropic's per-message effort (beta) and OpenAI's `configuration_update` (GPT-6) avoid it; neither is used. Model switches start a new cache on any design.
73	7. **Cache writes are not reported by TTL.** The Anthropic codec ignores `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m/1h_input_tokens`. That only matters once a 1-hour TTL is used. The Responses codec ignores `cache_write_tokens`, which only GPT-5.6+ reports and charges for.
74	8. **Lookback distance (low risk).** The moving Anthropic breakpoint is about 3 to 6 positions past the previous write in a normal turn: the response's thinking, text and calls, then the results. The window is 20 positions, and runs of `tool_use` or `tool_result` blocks count as one [A1]. A single response that interleaves more than about 18 thinking and call blocks would miss. Nothing seen so far comes close. A second moving breakpoint would cover it.
75	9. **OpenAI explicit mode (future).** If JusPrin moves to GPT-5.6+ and explicit mode turns out to be the default, a request without `prompt_cache_breakpoint` is not cached at all [O1]. The Responses codec places none. Check the default before switching models.
76	
77	Not a gap: the Anthropic tool and system breakpoints are at the end of fixed content, as recommended [A1]. Prompts are far above the minimum length (about 15,000 tokens of tools and system). The moving breakpoint follows the documented pattern. The Responses codec already gets `encrypted_content` with `store: false` by default [O2].

result.output:
## 1. Placement rules

Content-carrying system messages:

> A mid-conversation system message that carries content (`text`, `tool_addition`, or `tool_removal` blocks) must immediately follow a `user` turn (or an `assistant` turn ending in a server tool result), and must either be the last entry in `messages` or be immediately followed by an `assistant` turn. A `user` message that carries `tool_result` blocks counts: in an agentic loop you can place the system message right after the tool results, before Claude's next turn. Any other position for a message that carries content, including between an `assistant` `tool_use` block and the `tool_result` that answers it, returns a 400 error. A message with empty `content` that only sets [`output_config.effort`] is accepted anywhere in `messages`. Consecutive `system` messages are judged together, so an effort-only message next to one that carries content follows the rule for content.

Turn-scoped messages:

> A turn-scoped system message must follow a `user` turn (or an `assistant` turn ending in a server tool result) and precede an `assistant` turn or end the array, like any mid-conversation system message. One that ends the array always renders. One followed directly by another `user` message is a 400 error, not a cleared message.

Implications:
- A content-carrying system message cannot be first, cannot follow an `assistant` turn (other than one ending in a server tool result), and cannot sit between a `tool_use` and its `tool_result`.
- The page doesn't explicitly say whether two adjacent system messages are allowed. It only says consecutive system messages are judged together.

## 2. Shape, `clear_at`, and beta header

A system message is `"role": "system"` with `content` and, optionally, `clear_at`:

```json
{
  "role": "system",
  "clear_at": "next_user_message",
  "content": "Request independent reads in one turn."
}
```

> To scope a `role: "system"` message to the current turn, set its `clear_at` field. It takes one of two values:
> * `"never"` (the default): the message renders at its position on every request that includes it. Omitting the field is identical.
> * `"next_user_message"`: the message is **turn-scoped**. Its text renders only while no `role: "user"` message comes after it in `messages`.

Beta header: `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`.

> Turn-scoped system messages are in beta. Include the beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`. Without it, `clear_at` is rejected as an unknown field.

## 3. What clearing does and what must be re-sent

> Once a later user message exists, the message is **cleared**: it stays in the array but renders nothing and costs no input tokens, on that request and every later one.

> **Resend cleared messages verbatim.** A cleared message is still part of the conversation history. Rebuilding it from current state (a fresh token count, a timestamp), dropping it as redundant, or changing its `clear_at` value is an edit to an earlier message. On Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Haiku 5.5, every thinking block produced after it fails the prefix check.

So the message must stay in the array unchanged. Only its rendering stops.

## 4. `cache_control`

For turn-scoped messages, it is not allowed:

> **No `cache_control` on its blocks.** A cleared message is never part of a cache key, so a breakpoint on it could never match. Put the breakpoint on the last block of the preceding user turn instead.

The page doesn't state whether `cache_control` is allowed on a non-turn-scoped system message. The error list includes only the turn-scoped restriction.

## 5. Supported models

> This feature is available on Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Haiku 5.5. ... This feature is not available on Claude Sonnet 5. Use the top-level `system` field there instead.

The `supportedModels` metadata also lists `claude-mythos-preview`. Turn-scoped messages are in beta "on the same models and platforms as mid-conversation system messages."

## 6. `content` type

Plain string or array of blocks:

> Use a plain string or content blocks for `content`, the same as a `user` or `assistant` turn.

For turn-scoped messages, the constraint is narrower:

> **Text only.** `content` is one or more `text` blocks (or a string). `tool_addition` and `tool_removal` blocks return a 400 error on a turn-scoped message, and so does `output_config`. Use a separate `role: "system"` message without `clear_at` for those.

   The task came from another Claude Code session (id `local_34d95bfb-fc90-47e6-94ab-adc3d3711d01`), relayed as the first message. JusPrin, a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++17, wxWidgets), has an in-app Agent (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`). Today `AgentHost::make_agent_request` re-derives earlier turns on every request, and that breaks provider prompt caches. The task is step **R7** of the plan, which carries R2 (skills), R6 (notes), R4 (workspace blocks) and R5 (pictures):
   - Replace the re-derived history with an **append-only per-chat record**. Every request renders it byte for byte.
   - A record is bound to one wire format. Under D5 a model switch within the same format is allowed. A cross-format switch on an existing chat must be refused in `AgentHost::handle_set_chat_model` with a clear error.
   - The record holds every item sent: the person's messages with their workspace block, plate picture and file report; assistant output with thinking or reasoning verbatim; tool calls and results; fired skills; app notes.
   - Each item has a lifetime flag; items are never edited.
     - **R2, skills:** visible only on the request that fired them. On Anthropic this uses in-array `role:"system"` with `clear_at: "next_user_message"` and the beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`. On OpenAI a skill is a `developer` item that stays.
     - **Gateway exception:** send `clear_at` and the header only when the profile is not `account_sign_in`. Through the gateway, skills stay visible. This is decided per profile, never per request.
     - **R6, notes:** operator-role messages (Anthropic in-array `system`, OpenAI `developer`), kept visible, the same in the project and printer chats. This replaces the "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" user-text prefix.
     - Tool results stay in their own channel.
   - Pictures are stored as attachment-blob references and inlined at request time. Image bytes never go into `state.json`.
   - The record lives in the chat document (`ProjectStateDocument`/`ProjectPersistence`), so a reopened project renders the same bytes.
   - **Migration:** an old chat gets a one-time rendering of its old messages (plain person/assistant text, no tool replay) as its first record items. Do not keep the legacy builder. The commit message must say what an old chat's model now sees.
   - **Delete:** the `calls_by_message` replay, the text retelling, the note prefix, the stripping of workspace blocks and pictures, the skill dropping, and anything that only served them. Production code should shrink; any part that grows must be justified in its commit message.
   - **Tests (fake transports only):**
     - an item once sent never changes;
     - a later request is the earlier one plus appended items (modulo the moving `cache_control` breakpoint on the newest user message, never on a turn-scoped message);
     - a cross-format switch is refused;
     - an old chat migrates once;
     - a reopened project renders the same bytes.
     - Drop `[.]` from the two `[history-prefix]` guard cases, show them passing on both wire formats, and run the whole agent suite.
   - **Commits (at least):** R7 record and rendering (with R4/R5), R2 skill lifetime, R6 notes as operator, D5 cross-format refusal, un-hide the guard. Each message says what changed, why, and the production diff direction.
   - **Done means:** all commits on the branch; agent suite and guard green; an untracked `r7-report.md` in the worktree root. The report covers the design as built, migration behaviour, production diff stat, the gateway follow-up (add the header to the alias backend in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`), every difference in what the model now sees, and anything unverified.

   Rules and constraints (preserve):
   - Follow the AGENTS.md error-handling discipline: no catch-and-continue; invariant violations propagate.
   - **No live model calls at all.** Kenneth approves paid batches individually.
   - Commit on my branch only (`claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27`). No push, no merge. Never stage submodules. No attribution lines.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Prompt caching.**
     - Anthropic caches by byte-identical prefix: tools, then system, then messages. It uses cache_control breakpoints (on the last tool, on the system block, and a moving one on the newest user message's last block).
     - OpenAI uses implicit prefix caching plus `prompt_cache_key`, which is skipped for `account_sign_in`.
   - **Anthropic mid-conversation system messages** (doc fetched this session):
     - A content-carrying system message must immediately follow a user turn (a tool_result user message counts) and be last or followed by an assistant turn. Anything else returns 400.
     - `clear_at: "next_user_message"` makes a message turn-scoped. Once a later role:user message exists it renders nothing but must be re-sent verbatim. Changing `clear_at` or dropping the message counts as an edit, and every later thinking block then fails the prefix check.
     - A turn-scoped message followed directly by a user message is a 400.
     - `cache_control` is not allowed on a turn-scoped message.
     - Beta header: `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`.
     - Consecutive system messages are judged together. The doc does not say whether adjacent system messages are allowed.
     - Not supported on Sonnet 5.
   - **Existing `AnthropicCodec::normalized()`:**
     - merges adjacent same-role messages (system texts joined by "\n\n");
     - converts a system message that is not after a user message (or not followed by assistant or end) into a user text block.
   - **Gateway** (`account_sign_in`):
     - forwards messages and cache_control untouched;
     - sends only its configured headers;
     - on Responses, allows only `model, store, stream, parallel_tool_calls, instructions, tools, input, reasoning`.
   - **Record settlement rule (my design).** The loop hands items to the record only up to a "settled" point, from which a later request can still follow on:
     - after the turn's person-side items (unsent person messages, the turn's own message item with source);
     - after each Results item;
     - after an Assistant item with no calls (completion) or a pause_turn resend.
     - Trailing operator items (skills, notes) and skill pictures are not recorded until something follows them.
     - Record emission happens after a successful `transport->post()` and at completion.
     - This keeps the record free of trailing system messages (Anthropic placement) and of unanswered tool_use.
   - **Retry.** The turn's own message is already recorded, so `source` is empty and nothing person-side is added. Skills re-fire, and unrecorded notes become pending again.
   - **Turn item order:** unsent person messages; the turn's own user item (words, print_issue, workspace, attachments, images/PDF); then skill pictures (user items); then notes (operator); then skill texts (operator).
   - **Formats:** `wire_format(ProviderFamily)` returns `"anthropic"` or `"responses"`, reusing the `kFormatAnthropic`/`kFormatResponses` constants.
   - **D5 refusal design (planned):**
     - In handle_set_chat_model, compute the new format (account → `m_model_source->model_format`; otherwise the profile family). If the record is non-empty and the format differs, refuse.
     - Also refuse when switching to a profile that cannot clear (gateway) while the record has clearing items.
     - The refusal is sent as `kChatModel` with the unchanged choice plus `send_bridge_error`. The page shows bridge_error only as a diagnostic; this is a follow-up for the page.

   - **Planned R2 helper in ProviderProfile.hpp:** `clears_skills(profile)` = Anthropic && !account_sign_in. The clearing decision is stored per item (`RecordItem::clears`, set at append time from the profile). Send every chat from an append-only record of what it sent

Provider prompt caches (Anthropic and OpenAI) only reuse the part of a
request that opens with exactly the bytes of an earlier one. The host used
to rebuild a chat's earlier turns for every request in a shorter form:
plain text, calls replayed without the thinking around them, workspace
blocks and pictures stripped, skills dropped. So the start of the history
changed on every turn, and every turn paid full price for all of it.

Now each chat keeps a record in the project document of every item the
model was sent, and every request is that record followed by what the turn
has added so far:

- the person's messages, each with its print-issue context, workspace
  block, attachment listing, and picture or PDF parts as first sent; a
  file-load report as the turn's own words;
- the model's output exactly as the provider returned it, thinking or
  reasoning included (Responses items keep their ids);
- tool results in their own channel, pictures included;
- fired skills (their picture, then their text in the operator role) and
  the printer chat's notes as operator messages.

Items are only appended, never edited. ProviderAgent hands the host the
items a later request can follow on from: the person's side once a request
carrying it was accepted, each response with its results once the next
request went, the end of the turn when it completes. A trailing operator
message or a call without its result is never recorded. Picture and PDF
bytes go to blobs under attachments/chat-<id>/ beside the attachment
blobs; the document stores only their paths, and a reopened project reads
them back, so it renders the same bytes. Deleting a chat removes its blob
directory. A record is bound to the wire format it was written in; giving
it to the other format is a logic error (the model switch is refused
earlier in a following commit).

What an old chat's model now sees: a chat that talked before this change
gets a record the first time it talks again, once. It holds the person's
messages and file-load reports up to the last reply, and the replies, as
plain text. Its earlier tool calls and results, workspace blocks, pictures,
skills and notes were never kept and are not made up, so the model no
longer sees the earlier calls it used to get replayed. Messages after that
last reply go as any unsent message does.

Other differences in what the model sees:
- Skills stay in the record where they fired, on both formats (they used
  to be sent once on Responses, and kept within one turn only on
  Anthropic). A following commit makes Anthropic clear them.
- Earlier workspace blocks, pictures, attachments, and tool results with
  their workspace stay in later requests.
- An earlier tool result is now sent as Anthropic tool_result content
  blocks, the same as within a turn, instead of a plain string.
- A stopped or failed response's partial text and calls are not sent
  again; a message whose turn never reached the model still is.
- A title request sends the person's words only, without the chat.
- A retry whose turn the record already holds sends no new workspace.

transcript's opening/user_content/steps split and the codecs' separate

Show a fired skill on its own request only, on Anthropic

A skill the app fires (file loaded, slice failed, print issues, setup
changed) is meant for the request that fired it. With the chat record
every request repeats, removing it later would change the history before
the thinking that followed it. Anthropic's turn-scoped system message
solves this: a system message with clear_at "next_user_message" is shown
until the next user message and renders nothing after, while later
requests still send it unchanged, so the prefix stays the same.

- A fired skill's record item carries `clears` when the provider can
  clear it, decided per profile by clears_skills(): the Messages API
  directly, not JusPrin's gateway. The gateway sends only the headers it
  is configured with, so it cannot pass the beta header the field needs;
  through it skills stay visible, as they do on Responses, which has no
  such message.
- The Anthropic codec renders a clearing item as a system message with
  clear_at and sends `anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-
  2026-08-21` on every request of a profile that clears. It never merges
  a clearing system message with one that stays, judges a run of system
  messages together for placement (after a user message, last or before
  the assistant's), and still turns a run placed anywhere else into user
  text. Cache breakpoints go on user content only, never on a turn-scoped
  message.
- A turn's notes now sit after the fired skills' pictures and before
  their texts, so a note is not split from the skill by a user message
  (which would turn the note into user text).

What the model sees: on Anthropic, a skill fired in an earlier request
is no longer shown; through the gateway and on Responses it still is.

Unverified: whether the Messages API accepts a turn-scoped system message
directly after one that stays. The documentation judges consecutive
system messages together but does not say so outright. No live request
was made.

Production diff: +70/-28. It grows by the per-item flag, its storage,
the profile rule and the codec's handling of the new message shape.
EOF

     - a run of consecutive system messages is judged together;
     - `cache_control` is not allowed on them.

     - Results after posting the next request;

Send every chat from an append-only record of what it sent

Provider prompt caches (Anthropic and OpenAI) only reuse the part of a
request that opens with exactly the bytes of an earlier one. The host used
to rebuild a chat's earlier turns for every request in a shorter form:
plain text, calls replayed without the thinking around them, workspace
blocks and pictures stripped, skills dropped. So the start of the history
changed on every turn, and every turn paid full price for all of it.

Now each chat keeps a record in the project document of every item the
model was sent, and every request is that record followed by what the turn
has added so far:

- the person's messages, each with its print-issue context, workspace
  block, attachment listing, and picture or PDF parts as first sent; a
  file-load report as the turn's own words;
- the model's output exactly as the provider returned it, thinking or
  reasoning included (Responses items keep their ids);
- tool results in their own channel, pictures included;
- fired skills (their picture, then their text in the operator role) and
  the printer chat's notes as operator messages.

Items are only appended, never edited. ProviderAgent hands the host the
items a later request can follow on from: the person's side once a request
carrying it was accepted, each response with its results once the next
request went, the end of the turn when it completes. A trailing operator
message or a call without its result is never recorded. Picture and PDF
bytes go to blobs under attachments/chat-<id>/ beside the attachment
blobs; the document stores only their paths, and a reopened project reads
them back, so it renders the same bytes. Deleting a chat removes its blob
directory. A record is bound to the wire format it was written in; giving
it to the other format is a logic error (the model switch is refused
earlier in a following commit).

What an old chat's model now sees: a chat that talked before this change
gets a record the first time it talks again, once. It holds the person's
messages and file-load reports up to the last reply, and the replies, as
plain text. Its earlier tool calls and results, workspace blocks, pictures,
skills and notes were never kept and are not made up, so the model no
longer sees the earlier calls it used to get replayed. Messages after that
last reply go as any unsent message does.

Other differences in what the model sees:
- Skills stay in the record where they fired, on both formats (they used
  to be sent once on Responses, and kept within one turn only on
  Anthropic). A following commit makes Anthropic clear them.
- Earlier workspace blocks, pictures, attachments, and tool results with
  their workspace stay in later requests.
- An earlier tool result is now sent as Anthropic tool_result content
  blocks, the same as within a turn, instead of a plain string.
- A stopped or failed response's partial text and calls are not sent
  again; a message whose turn never reached the model still is.
- A title request sends the person's words only, without the chat.
- A retry whose turn the record already holds sends no new workspace.

Deleted: the host's history rebuild (its calls_by_message replay, the
retelling of reports and notes, the workspace and skill stripping), the
transcript's opening/user_content/steps split and the codecs' separate
paths for them, and tool_output_json, which only existed to share code
with the replay.

# R7: every chat sends an append-only record of what it sent

Branch `claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27`, five commits on `0807d77282`, not pushed or merged.
Each request a chat sends now starts with the exact bytes of its previous request, so the
provider's prompt cache can reuse the earlier part on both Anthropic Messages and OpenAI
Responses. The agent suite passes (16777 assertions in 479 test cases, random order), and the
two history-prefix guard cases now run by default and pass on both wire formats.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `ba08e2c18f` | R7: the per-chat record replaces the rebuilt history |
| `fe70eea593` | R2: a fired skill clears at the next user message on Anthropic (not through the gateway) |
| `f5039d09e8` | R6: app notes are operator messages in project and printer chats |
| `59304a1ef9` | D5: a chat that has talked refuses a model in the other wire format |
| `9fce6ddb2b` | The `[history-prefix]` guard runs by default (test-only) |

No live model calls were made. Everything below was checked with fake transports only.

## Design as built

**The record.** `ProjectStateDocument` keeps a `ChatRecord {format, items}` per chat. `format`
is `"anthropic"` or `"responses"` and is fixed by the first append. Each `RecordItem` is one of:

- `User`: the person's message as sent (words, print-issue context, workspace block, attachment
  listing, pictures and PDFs as parts). `source` is the message id.
- `Operator`: a fired skill's text or an app note. `clears` is set on skills that the provider
  can hide later (R2).
- `Assistant`: the provider's output item exactly as returned, thinking/reasoning included;
  Responses items keep their ids.
- `Results`: tool results, in the tool-result channel, pictures included.

Items are only appended. `append_chat_record` checks the format and builds all entries before
changing anything, so a bad append leaves the record untouched. Picture and PDF bytes are written
as blobs under `attachments/chat-<id>/<request_id>-<n>`; state.json holds only the paths, and a
reopened project reads the same bytes back. Deleting a chat removes that directory.

**When items are kept.** `ProviderAgent` reports items through `AgentRequest::on_recorded` only
once a later request can safely follow on from them:

- the person's side, once a request carrying it was accepted;
- a response and its results, once the next request was posted;
- the final response, when the turn completes.

A trailing operator item (skill or note) is kept only once a response follows it, and a call is
never kept without its result. In a turn the app starts with a note, the turn's workspace block
and the note are kept together after the model answers, so a failed request leaves neither
behind.

**Request order.** Each request is built as:

1. the record;
2. person messages not yet sent;
3. the turn's own user item (an empty-worded workspace item in an app turn);
4. fired skills' pictures;
5. notes (unsent ones, then the turn's note);
6. fired skills' texts.

A retry of a turn the record already holds adds no new workspace block. A record given to the
other wire format throws `logic_error`; D5 stops that from being reachable.

**Codecs.** Both codecs now render one list of record items instead of the old
opening/user_content/steps split.

- Anthropic: operator items become system messages in the conversation. Clearing ones carry
  `clear_at: "next_user_message"` and the request carries `anthropic-beta:
  mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`. A clearing and a non-clearing system message
  are never merged. A run of system messages is judged together for placement (after a user
  message, and last or before the assistant's); any run placed elsewhere becomes user text. The
  moving cache breakpoint stays on the newest user message and never goes on a turn-scoped
  system message.
- Responses: operator items become `developer` items, assistant output is inserted verbatim,
  and results become `function_call_output` items followed by user picture messages.

**Skills clear per profile, never per request.** `clears_skills(profile)` is true for the
Anthropic family unless the profile is `account_sign_in` (JusPrin's gateway).

**D5.** `handle_set_chat_model` refuses a model whose format differs from the record's, and
refuses the gateway for a chat whose record has clearing skills. The chat keeps its model, the
page gets its unchanged choice back, and a `bridge_error` with code `chat_format_fixed` says to
start a new chat. A chat with no record takes any model. The same check runs when a turn starts,
because a chat's choice can change under it (for example a provider's key is removed). In that
case the turn fails with the same message.

## Migration of chats from before this change

A chat that talked before this change gets a record the first time it talks again, once. The
record is in that turn's wire format and holds, as plain text only:

- the person's messages and file-load reports up to the last earlier reply that had text;
- the replies.

Earlier tool calls and results, workspace blocks, pictures, skills and notes were never stored,
so they are not made up. Messages after that last reply go as any unsent message does. A chat
with no earlier reply gets no migration.
