## Gateway follow-up

JusPrin's gateway sends only the headers it is configured with. Until it passes
`anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`, `account_sign_in` profiles do not
clear skills, so a fired skill stays visible in every later request.

To enable clearing through the gateway:

1. Add the header to the Anthropic alias backend in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` on the server.
2. Make `clears_skills()` in `ProviderProfile.hpp` return true for `account_sign_in` too.
3. Relax D5's gateway refusal in `record_refusal` in `AgentHost.cpp`.

## Every difference in what the model sees

- **Earlier turns.** They are sent exactly as first sent:
  - workspace blocks, attachment listings, pictures and PDFs stay in later requests (they used
    to be stripped);
  - thinking/reasoning and Responses item ids stay;
  - tool calls and results stay in their own channels.
- **Earlier tool results on Anthropic** are `tool_result` content blocks, as within a turn, not a
  plain string.
- **Skills.** A skill stays where it fired.
  - Anthropic direct: hidden after the next user message (`clear_at`).
  - Responses and the gateway: still visible in later requests. Before, a skill was sent once on
    Responses and kept within one turn only on Anthropic.
- **Notes.** Notes are operator messages (Anthropic system, Responses developer) with no
  "JusPrin app note, not the person's words:" prefix. The project chat now sees its notes, which
  it did not before.
  - On Anthropic, a note with nothing from the person before it (a printer chat turn the app
    started) still becomes user text, as the API requires.
  - A note rewritten after it was sent (Undo on a saved-preset receipt) is sent again as it now
    reads.
- **Order within a turn.** Skill pictures, then notes, then skill texts.
- **Stopped or failed responses.** Their partial text and calls are not sent again. A message
  whose turn never reached the model still is.
- **Title requests** send only the person's words, without the chat.
- **Retries** of a turn the record already holds send no new workspace block.
- **Migrated chats.** Earlier words and replies go as plain text. The earlier tool calls that
  used to be replayed are gone.
- **Wire-format switch.** A chat that has talked cannot switch to a model in the other wire
  format, or to the gateway once it has clearing skills. The person has to start a new chat.

## Unverified

- **Anthropic run of system messages.** Unverified whether the Messages API accepts a turn-scoped
  (`clear_at`) system message directly after one that stays. The docs judge a run of system
  messages together but do not say so outright.
- **Responses item ids.** Unverified whether Responses accepts verbatim output items with ids
  (reasoning, message, function_call) from earlier turns when `store:false`. If it rejects them,
  the record must drop ids or keep `encrypted_content`.
- **Wire bytes on a real provider.** No live request was made, so the actual request bytes and
  cache hits were not checked against a real provider. The guard proves byte-identical prefixes
  only against the codecs' own output.
- **Shell harness build.** `tests/shell` and `tests/project_prompt` were not built here (only
  `agent_bridge_tests`). A grep found no use of the removed fields there.
- **Page behaviour on refusal.** The page shows `bridge_error` only as a diagnostic, so after a
  refused model switch the person sees the picker reset without the reason.

## Follow-ups outside this branch's scope

- `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (lines ~900, 980, 987, 989): `CalibrationAgent` recognises app
  turns by the old "JusPrin app note, not the person's words:" prefix in `user_text`. It must
  read `request.note` instead, or those harness scenarios stop matching. The sibling session that
  owns `tests/shell` should make this change.
- The Agent page should show `chat_format_fixed` to the person.
- Gateway header and the two code switches, listed under "Gateway follow-up" above.

content.text:
All five commits are on `claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27`:

- `ba08e2c18f` (R7): each chat keeps an append-only record and resends it byte for byte.
- `fe70eea593` (R2): a fired skill clears at the next user message on direct Anthropic, but not through the gateway.
- `f5039d09e8` (R6): app notes become operator messages in both chats.
- `59304a1ef9` (D5): a chat that has talked refuses a model in the other wire format.
- `9fce6ddb2b`: the two `[history-prefix]` guard cases now run by default.

The agent suite passes (16777 assertions in 479 test cases, random order). The guard passes on both Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses. Everything used fake transports; there were no live model calls, and nothing is pushed or merged.

The full write-up is in [r7-report.md](r7-report.md), untracked in the worktree root. It covers:

- the design as built;
- migration: an old chat's earlier words and replies go once, as plain text;
- the production diff;
- the gateway follow-up;
- every change in what the model sees;
- what is unverified.

Points to act on:

- **Production code grew, it did not shrink:** +713/−352 in `src/`, net +361. Most of it is the record's storage and the code that decides when items are kept. Each commit message says where it grew and why.
- **Gateway:** add the header `anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21` to the Anthropic alias backend in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`. Then turn on `clears_skills()` for `account_sign_in` profiles and relax the gateway refusal in D5.
- **Shell harness:** `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` still finds app turns by the old "JusPrin app note…" prefix in `user_text`, at lines ~900–989. It must read `request.note` instead. That folder belongs to the sibling session, so I left a note in the shared notes folder (`r7-record.md`) and did not build or edit it.
- **Unverified:**
  - whether Anthropic accepts a `clear_at` system message directly after one that stays;
  - whether Responses accepts earlier output items with their ids when `store:false`.
- **Page:** after a refused model switch, the picker resets without saying why, because the page only logs `bridge_error`.

1. CONFIRMED. Every migrated chat throws on its first request. start_chat_record stores the migrated record with format "" (ProjectStateDocument.cpp:916). ProviderAgent::begin_transcript (ProviderAgent.cpp:239) throws logic_error whenever items are non-empty and format != wire_format(family), so "" fails on both providers, on that message and every later one. The migration test uses RecordingAgent, not ProviderAgent, and asserts the empty format, so it records exactly the input that crashes the real loop. Fix: the migration stamps the turn's wire format (it already knows it), and the test runs the real ProviderAgent with a fake transport over a migrated chat. While there, the same format invariant is checked in three layers (record_refusal in the host, begin_transcript in the agent, append_chat_record in the document); keep the document's check plus the host's refusal and drop the agent's, per AGENTS.md "no duplicated defensive checks".

2. CONFIRMED. The version-store prune deletes every picture and PDF the record keeps. Blobs go to attachments/chat-<conv>/<request>-<n> (ProjectStateDocument.hpp:114, AgentHost.cpp:2766). ProjectVersionStore::prune, run from ProjectAutosave::trim_history after every version, removes every regular file under attachments/ that is not in the document's attachments index (ProjectVersionStore.cpp, final loop). Chat blobs are in neither the index nor live_attachments. Afterwards load_record_bytes gets "" from read_attachment_blob (missing file returns empty) and the next request carries an image block with empty data, permanently, since the record is append-only. Also: a forked managed identity copies only the opened file's attachment folder, so chat blobs are not carried over. Fix: either keep chat blobs somewhere prune never sweeps (own top-level directory in the managed folder, carried on fork and deleted with the chat) or make them part of what prune keeps; and make a missing blob an invariant violation that throws, never an empty picture. Test it through on-disk persistence with the autosave/prune path, not in-memory.

3. CONFIRMED. The record is appended when the transport accepts the post (ProviderAgent.cpp:406, record() right after m_transport->post returns true), not when the provider accepts the request. A 413 or a 400 for a bad or oversized picture then leaves the person's message, workspace block and pictures in the record and the chat can never send again. Fix: append only once the provider has answered 2xx (first stream event or completion), so a rejected request leaves no trace; the "a turn whose request fails" test must distinguish a 503 (message kept, nothing recorded) from a 400/413 (same). Also do the fallible blob write before dispatch, not inside on_recorded after the request is in flight; today an exception there leaves m_busy true with a live request.

4. UNVERIFIED, needs a live check before merge, which Kenneth has to approve (do not make the call yourself): Responses reasoning items are replayed across turns with their ids under store:false and no encrypted_content (ResponsesCodec.cpp:72-76, :155; no include requested). Community reports describe a 404 "Item … not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false" for exactly this. If true, the failure is permanent per chat. Read OpenAI's current Responses docs on store:false, reasoning items and include=reasoning.encrypted_content and say what the record must keep for replay to be valid; make the codec change if the docs settle it, and say what a live two-turn check should look for.

Smaller findings, fix if cheap and say which you skipped: retrying a failed reply that is not the newest sends a request ending on an assistant item (make_agent_request early return on empty source, AgentHost.cpp:2967; handle_retry does not require the newest message); turn_recorded re-derives "already sent" from attempt>1 && source.empty() when the host knows it exactly via sent(id); a rewritten note is re-sent only when it starts the turn, and each re-send appends a duplicate id to record.messages (ProjectStateDocument.cpp:902); the record is read leniently (value() defaults, unknown part kinds become PDFs) while written strictly, so read with at() and throw on unknown kinds; a reply request with no on_recorded sink is a silent no-op in record() (ProviderAgent.cpp:329), it should throw; each turn start parses the whole record three times and re-reads and base64-encodes every blob on the GUI thread, parse once per turn and avoid the encode/decode round trip if RecordPart holds bytes.

Summarise the problem and the resolution: what error happens when reasoning items are replayed with store=false, does including encrypted_content fix it, and must the id be kept or stripped? Quote the error message text exactly if given.

result.output:
**Problem:** With `store=False`, the poster couldn't carry reasoning forward. Passing `reasoning=` as a request parameter was rejected, and appending the reasoning object as a message with a custom role was not allowed. Replaying the reasoning item in `input` without the rest of the output also failed. One user got this error: "of type 'reasoning' was provided without its required following item."

**Resolution:** Add the items from `response.output` to `input` in their original shape, rather than building role-based messages. One user did this with `inputs.extend(response_1.output)` before appending the next user message. The reasoning item must be followed by its paired message item.

**Does `encrypted_content` fix the error?** The thread doesn't establish this. The error was resolved by keeping the reasoning and following message items intact. Whether `encrypted_content` is needed in the replayed item isn't settled. The schema lists it as nullable, and one user said the `include` parameter is optional on the return path, but that claim wasn't tested.

**Keep or strip the `id`?** Keep it. The thread's schema summary lists `id` as required for reasoning input items, and one user reported that exact copies, including IDs, were needed to avoid the error. One commenter speculated that made-up IDs might be tolerated, but this was posed as a question, not confirmed.

# R7: every chat sends an append-only record of what it sent

Each request a chat sends now starts with the exact bytes of its previous request, so the
provider's prompt cache can reuse the earlier part on Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses.

A review found four blocking problems. Three are fixed in `17300104a0`, each with a test that
fails without its fix. The fourth (Responses reasoning items) is settled from OpenAI's current
docs, but needs a live check that Kenneth must approve.

Test results:

- Agent suite: 17152 assertions in 486 test cases, random order.
- History-prefix guard: 178 assertions in 4 test cases, on both wire formats.
- No live model calls were made.

The work is on branch `claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27`: six commits on `0807d77282`. Nothing is
pushed or merged.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `ba08e2c18f` | R7: the per-chat record replaces the rebuilt history |
| `fe70eea593` | R2: a fired skill clears at the next user message on Anthropic (not through the gateway) |
| `f5039d09e8` | R6: app notes are operator messages in project and printer chats |
| `59304a1ef9` | D5: a chat that has talked refuses a model in the other wire format |
| `9fce6ddb2b` | The `[history-prefix]` guard runs by default (test-only) |
| `17300104a0` | Review fixes: record only what the provider took, keep pictures out of prune's reach, stamp the migration's format |

The `17300104a0` message gives that commit's production diff as "+274/-226". The real figure is
+267/−219; the net +48 is correct. The commit was not amended, because the git policy requires
confirmation first.

## Design as built

### The record

`ProjectStateDocument` keeps a `ChatRecord` per chat with three fields:

- `format`: `"anthropic"` or `"responses"`. It is fixed by the first stored items and never empty.
- `items`: everything the chat sent, in order.
- `migrated`: the message ids a migration covered (see below).

Each `RecordItem` is one of four kinds:

- `User`: the person's message as sent (words, a `<print_issue>` block, the workspace block, the
  attachment listing, pictures and PDFs). Its `source` is the message id.
- `Operator`: a fired skill's text or an app note. `clears` is set on skills the provider can hide
  later (R2).
- `Assistant`: the provider's output exactly as returned, thinking or reasoning included. Responses
  items keep their ids.
- `Results`: tool results, in the provider's tool-result channel, pictures included.

`ChatRecord::holds(id)` answers "was this message sent?" from the items' sources plus the
`migrated` ids. The record is read strictly: missing fields and unknown kinds throw. Items are only
appended, and `append_chat_record` checks everything before it changes anything.

### Pictures and PDFs

These are stored as blobs under `chats/<conversation>/<request_id>-<n>`, relative to the JusPrin
data dir. Each blob holds the base64 text exactly as sent, so neither writing nor reading decodes
or re-encodes. state.json stores only the blob paths.

The folder is a top-level `chats/`, not under `attachments/`. `ProjectVersionStore::prune` removes
every file under `attachments/` that the document's attachment index does not name. Prune runs
after every version (from `ProjectAutosave::trim_history`) and never reads chat records.

The folder is deleted with its chat, in managed projects too: `remove_attachment_dir` still skips
`attachments/` folders there, because published versions can reference them. Importing an archive
copies `chats/` alongside `attachments/`. A blob missing when a turn starts throws a
`RuntimeError`, instead of sending an empty picture on every later request.

### When items join the record

`ProviderAgent` hands items to `AgentRequest::on_recorded` at the provider's first stream event for
a request, when everything before `m_settled` is appended.

- A request the provider refuses (503, 400, 413, or any transport error) leaves nothing behind.
- Within a turn, items settle at these points:
  - the person's side, once its request is taken;
  - a response together with its results, once the next request is taken;
  - the final response, at completion.
- A trailing operator item (a skill or note) and a call without its result are never stored.
- In an app turn (one started by a note), the turn's workspace item and the note are settled
  together.

Each picture's blob is written through `AgentRequest::keep_blob` before the request that first
sends it. If a blob cannot be written, the request is never sent and the turn fails with the
existing generic error. A reply request with no sinks is a `logic_error`. `AgentSetup`'s key check
is not a chat, so it passes no-op sinks.

### Request order

Each request is built in this order:

1. the record;
2. the person's messages not yet sent;
3. the turn's own user item (with no source in an app turn);
4. fired skills' pictures;
5. notes (unsent notes, then the turn's note);
6. fired skills' texts.

The host hands the loop ready-made `RecordItem`s for unsent messages. The host also sets
`turn_recorded` when the record already holds the turn's message (a retry); the loop then adds no
new workspace block. The migration and the unsent loop share one message-to-item function
(`as_sent`).

### Codecs

- Anthropic: operator items become system messages. Clearing ones carry
  `clear_at: "next_user_message"`, and the request carries the header
  `anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`. Placement is judged per run of
  system messages, and a misplaced run becomes user text.
- Responses: operator items become `developer` items, output is replayed verbatim, and results are
  `function_call_output` items followed by user messages with the pictures.

### D5: switching wire formats

`set_chat_model` refuses a model whose format differs from the record's. It also refuses the
gateway for a chat whose record holds clearing skills. The refusal sends `chat_format_fixed` as a
`bridge_error`. The same check runs at turn start, against the record read once for that turn.

### Retry

Only the chat's last reply can be retried. Retrying an earlier failed reply now gets
`invalid_retry`. Before, it sent a request that ended on an assistant item.

## Migration of chats from before the record

The first turn of an older chat builds its record in memory from the messages up to the last
earlier reply with text, as plain text:

- the person's words, with a `<print_issue>` block where the message had one;
- file-load reports;
- the replies.

Notes, calls, results, workspace blocks and pictures were never stored, so they are not made up.
The covered ids go into `migrated`. Messages after the last reply go as any unsent message does.

The migrated record is stored together with the first items the provider takes, in the format of
that request. This fixed the bug where every migrated chat threw on its first request: the old
migration stored format `""`, and the loop refused any record whose format differed from the
provider's.

The migration test now runs the real `ProviderAgent` on both wire formats, and checks two things:

- the earlier words go exactly once;
- the next turn opens with the migrated turn's request.

## Responses reasoning items under store:false (blocker 4)

OpenAI's reasoning guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning, read
2026-10-29) states three things:

- In stateless mode (`store:false` or Zero Data Retention), reasoning items in a response's
  `output` "include an `encrypted_content` property by default".
- The `include` value `reasoning.encrypted_content` is a legacy value, still accepted "for
  compatibility, but doesn't require it".
- Items should be passed into the next request "untouched", and the complete history replayed.

For replay to be valid, the record must keep every output item exactly as returned: the reasoning
item with its `id` and `encrypted_content`, the message items (with any `phase`), and the
`function_call` items. It already does, so the codec is unchanged. I did not add `include`, because
JusPrin's gateway refuses fields it does not list.

The 404 "Items are not persisted when store is set to false" reported on community.openai.com
matches a reasoning item replayed without `encrypted_content`. Under the current docs that should
not happen.

The live check needs Kenneth's approval. It is a two-turn chat on a reasoning model with `effort`
set, through the app, on OpenAI directly, and if possible also through OpenRouter and the gateway.
It should confirm three things:

1. Turn 1's response holds a `reasoning` item with a non-null `encrypted_content`.
2. Turn 2's request carries that item byte for byte.
3. Turn 2 succeeds with no 404 and no "Item … not found". Ideally `cached_tokens` is above zero.

The same replay already happened within a turn before R7, whenever a tool call was followed by its
result.

## Every difference in what the model sees

- **Earlier turns** are sent exactly as first sent:
  - workspace blocks, attachment listings, pictures and PDFs stay in later requests (they used to
    be stripped);
  - thinking or reasoning stays, and Responses items keep their ids;
  - tool calls and results stay in their own channels.
- **Earlier tool results on Anthropic** are `tool_result` content blocks, not a plain string.
- **Skills** stay where they fired:
  - straight to Anthropic, the provider hides them after the next user message;
  - on Responses and through the gateway, they stay visible.
- **Notes** are operator messages (Anthropic system, Responses developer) with no "JusPrin app
  note…" prefix. The project chat now sees its notes, which it did not see before. A note rewritten
  after it was sent (Undo on a receipt) goes again as it now reads, whichever turn comes next.
- **Order within a turn**: skill pictures, then notes, then skill texts.
- **Refused or failed requests** (new in the review fixes):
  - A refused request leaves nothing behind, and the person's message goes again with the next
    turn.
  - When a later request of a turn is refused or fails, the calls the model made in that turn are
    not stored. The next turn sees the person's message and the current workspace, not those
    calls.
  - A stopped or failed response's partial text is not sent again.
- **Retries**:
  - A retry after the provider took the turn's request sends that request again, byte for byte.
  - Only the chat's last reply can be retried.
- **Title requests** send only the person's words.
- **Migrated chats**: earlier words and replies go once, as plain text, with any print-issue block.
- **Format switch**: a chat that has talked cannot switch to a model in the other wire format, or
  to the gateway once it has clearing skills.

Commit 17300104a0 on `claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27` fixes all four review blockers. The branch now has six commits: ba08e2c18f R7, fe70eea593 R2, f5039d09e8 R6, 59304a1ef9 D5, 9fce6ddb2b guard, 17300104a0 fixes. Nothing is pushed. The agent suite passes (17152 assertions, random order) and so does the history-prefix guard. No live model calls were made.

The four blockers:

1. **Migrated chats threw on their first request.** The migrated record is now stored in the request's format, together with the first items the provider accepts. The agent's duplicate format check is gone. The test runs the real ProviderAgent on both wire formats.
2. **The version-store prune deleted chat pictures.** They now live in a top-level `chats/<conversation>/` folder, which prune never sweeps. Importing a project copies the folder, deleting a chat removes it (managed projects too), and a missing picture throws.
3. **The record grew as soon as the transport accepted the post.** It now grows at the provider's first stream event, and pictures are written to disk before the request goes out. Tests check that a 503, 400 or 413 leaves nothing in the record, including when a later request of a turn is refused.
4. **Responses reasoning replay under `store:false`.** OpenAI's reasoning guide says stateless responses carry `encrypted_content` by default and that output items are replayed untouched. The record already keeps them byte for byte, so the codec is unchanged. A live two-turn check (needs Kenneth's approval) should confirm:
   - turn 1's reasoning item has `encrypted_content`;
   - turn 2's request carries that item verbatim;
   - turn 2 gets no 404.

The smaller findings and trims are done, including the rule that only a chat's last reply can be retried. Each new test failed with its fix removed.

**Commit message is wrong.** 17300104a0's message gives its production diff as +274/−226. The real figure is +267/−219; the net +48 is right. I did not amend it, because amending needs your confirmation.

**Diff since the base:** production code is 15 files, +779/−370 lines; tests are +1255/−330.

- the real prune, because libslic3r is not built in this worktree, so the test applies prune's rule for `attachments/` itself;
- whether an exported managed archive carries `chats/`;
- the Responses replay, which is checked against the docs only, not live;
- `tests/shell`, which was not built here.

`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` still matches the old app-note prefix. A note about it is in the shared notes folder for the session that owns `tests/shell`.

Everything is written up in `r7-report.md` in the worktree root, which stays untracked.

Yes, I'd expect that too, and it didn't happen. Since the branch base, production code is up 409 lines net (+779/−370). Sending what a chat sent before, unchanged, should mostly delete code.

Where the 409 lines went, by file:

| Area | Net lines | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Codecs (`AnthropicCodec`, `ResponsesCodec`, `ProviderCodec.hpp`) | −33 | The rebuilt history is gone. This is the only part that shrank. |
| `ProjectStateDocument` | +236 | New record types plus their JSON reading and writing. |
| `AgentHost` | +124 | Migration of older chats, picture files, the model-switch refusal, the retry rule. |
| `ProviderAgent` | +105 | Tracking which items the provider has taken, and writing pictures. |
| Smaller files | about −23 | Profile flags, persistence, setup sinks. |

Two of the side features aren't simplification at all:
- Hiding a fired skill after the next message, on Anthropic: +42 lines.
- The refusal to switch a chat to a model in the other wire format: +38 lines.

The biggest waste is a design choice I made. I gave the record its own neutral item types (`RecordItem`, `RecordPart`), and each codec translates them to its provider's JSON on every request. That made sense only while a chat could change wire format. The same branch now forbids that switch, so a chat only ever talks to one format, and the record could just be that provider's own message JSON, appended as sent.

That would remove:
- the record types and their JSON reading and writing;
- the item-kind table;
- the codec code that turns record items into wire JSON.

It would keep the append, the picture files and the check on which items the provider has taken. My estimate, not yet measured, is about 200 fewer lines. That would bring the branch to roughly +200 net, most of it storage that has to exist somewhere. Migration of older chats (about 70 lines) is the other large piece. Cutting it is your call, because old chats would then start without their earlier conversation.
We don't need migrations. What are the other scope creep that you sneaked into this task?

## R2 design point from the R8 breakpoint analysis (settled: see the end of this section)

Anthropic's `clear_at: "next_user_message"` clears at the next `role:"user"` message, and a message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts. So under R2 a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, not for the rest of the turn. That matches today's Responses codec (which drops the skill from the next request) and not today's Anthropic codec (which keeps it visible for the turn). If "cleared at the next user message" was meant as the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that. **My call (2026-10-29, not Kenneth's; he can override):** a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, on both providers. Reasons: it is what the OpenAI path does today and what the prompt evals were run against; `clear_at` gives it for free; the alternative needs skills kept in the record for the whole chat, which the lifetime design exists to avoid. R2 implements this; the Anthropic path loses rest-of-turn visibility, which the evals after R2 will show if it matters. Also: `cache_control` is a 400 on a turn-scoped message, so breakpoint 3 (last block of the newest user message) stays where it is; the skill-text leak then disappears on its own because a cleared message costs no input tokens and is never written to the cache. content.text:
<cross-session-message from="local_8f4ebb21-2ad3-4882-8c94-0723919a89da" from-name="Chat history cache handoff">
Kenneth looked at the R7 branch's net +409 production lines and asks which parts are really necessary given that this version has not been released to anyone. His words: "Tell the session to check for unnecessary scope creep and trim them." Treat every piece below as suspect until it earns its lines, with these premises: there are no users with existing chats, so a chat recorded before the record may simply start a fresh record (no migration); the only acceptance tests are the history-prefix guard on both wire formats, the agent suite, and the design rules (append-only record, lifetime flags, pictures as blob references, one wire format per chat).

Go through each and either delete it or justify it in one sentence with the failure it prevents today:
- Migration of chats from before the record: delete, start fresh.
- The chats/<conversation>/ blob folder with its import/delete/fork handling: can the record reference the existing attachment store (pictures the person attached are already blobs there; plate pictures and skill pictures may be the only new bytes) instead of a second store? If a second store is unavoidable, keep the smallest version.
- The settlement rule (items join at first stream event, blob writes before dispatch, trailing operator items kept only once a response follows): keep what is needed so a refused request leaves no trace and a later request is the earlier plus appended items; delete bookkeeping beyond that.
- Strict reading with at() and throws on unknown kinds: keep only if it is fewer lines than the lenient version, otherwise keep whichever is shorter.
- The cross-format refusal (D5): the decision stands, but implement it in one place, at the model picker, not also at turn start, unless a test shows the picker alone is insufficient.
- Retry rules, rewritten-note resend, record parsed once per turn: keep only what a test on the branch needs.
- Anything in the codecs that exists for a case the record can no longer produce.

Then report: production diff stat before and after the trim, a table of what was deleted with the line count each, what you kept and why, and the suite and guard results. Same rules: own branch commits, no live calls, no push, build rules as before. If you believe something Kenneth may see as scope creep is in fact required by the design rules, say so plainly rather than keeping it quietly.
</cross-session-message>

  history. The turn the app starts on its own note still sends the
  note as it reads now, because a receipt's Undo rewrites the note and
  starts a turn on it to tell the model.
- The refusal of JusPrin Cloud for chats with fired skills is gone.
  The record marks every fired skill as clearing; the Anthropic codec
  adds clear_at only where the provider can clear it (straight to
  Anthropic), and the skill stays in place through the gateway.
- The wire-format check (decision D5) runs in one place, at the start
  of a turn. That covers both a model the person picked and the default
  a removed key falls back to; the picker no longer refuses.
- The codecs no longer render plain-text replies, which only migration
  produced.

The agent suite and the [history-prefix] guard pass.

## Trim (`1849db0fdc`, 2026-10-29)

The branch had reached +409 net production lines. Kenneth asked for scope creep to be cut: there
are no released users, so a chat from before the record simply starts a fresh one. The trim removed
−270/+62 lines in `src/`. The branch is now 15 files, +572/−371 against `0807d77282`: net +201, down
from +409. The agent suite passes (17033 assertions in 483 test cases) and so does the guard (178
assertions in 4 test cases).

### Deleted

The line counts are approximate, assigned by diff hunk.

| What | Net lines |
|---|---|
| Hand-written JSON reading and writing of record items, replaced by nlohmann's type macros (reads still throw on a missing field; an unknown kind name is no longer an error) | about −88 |
| Migration of chats from before the record: `record_of_earlier_chat`, `start_chat_record`, `ChatRecord::migrated`, the shared pending-migration sink, and the codecs' plain-text reply paths | about −75 |
| The format check in two places (model picker and turn start) plus the gateway refusal for chats with fired skills, replaced by one check at turn start | about −23 |
| Re-sending a rewritten note inside earlier history | about −6 |
| Comments | rest |

### Kept, with the failure each prevents today

- **The record's own picture store, `chats/<conversation>/`.** Pictures cannot point at the
  attachment files: the app shrinks every attached image before sending it (`m_image_for_model`),
  so the bytes the model saw are not the file on disk. Tool and skill pictures have no attachment
  at all. Prune deletes anything under `attachments/` missing from the attachment index, so the
  store sits outside it.
- **Writing pictures before the request goes out (`keep_blob`).** A write that failed after the
  provider had accepted the request would leave the turn either hung or silently missing items. A
  write that fails first fails the turn cleanly.
- **Settlement.** A refused request leaves no trace, and each later request is the earlier one
  plus appended items. Without it, a 400 or 413 would stay in the chat for good.
- **Only the chat's last reply can be retried.** The page shows Retry on every failed reply
  (`MessageList.tsx`). Retrying an earlier one whose message the record holds would send a request
  ending on the model's own reply.
- **A turn the app starts with its own note always sends the note as it reads now.** A receipt's
  Undo rewrites the note and starts a turn on it to tell the model. The existing Undo test failed
  without this rule.
- **The format check at turn start, not at the picker.** A removed API key moves the chat to the
  default provider without the picker running; a test covers that. The turn-start failure shows in
  the chat, while the picker's error went only to the page's diagnostics.

### Model-visible changes from the trim

- A chat with no record sends its earlier person messages and notes once, as messages not yet
  sent, with no replies. Only development data has such chats.
- Through JusPrin Cloud, a fired skill stays in place; its `clear_at` is left out instead of the
  switch being refused. A chat that moves between direct Anthropic and the gateway pays one cold
  cache.
- A note rewritten after the model read it is not re-sent, except when the app starts a turn on
  it (Undo).
- Picking a model in another wire format no longer refuses at the picker; the next turn fails with
  `chat_format_fixed`.
